findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/Probability/HasLaw.lean:171 `lemma HasLaw.integral_comp ... (hX : HasLaw X μ P) (hf : AEStronglyMeasurable f μ) : P[f ∘ X] = ∫ x, f x ∂μ`, proved by `rw [← hX.map_eq, integral_map hX.aemeasurable, Function.comp_def]` — the same proof as lines 244-245 here.
findings.fix: Delete `integral_fourier_comp`; add `public import Mathlib.Probability.HasLaw` and at its three use sites (lines 258, 272) write `hX.integral_comp (fourier n).continuous.aestronglyMeasurable`.
findings.issue: `integral_fourier_comp` is `ProbabilityTheory.HasLaw.integral_comp` specialized to `f = fourier n` (the RHS `anisotropyCoeff μ n` is `∫ x, fourier n x ∂μ` by rfl), and its proof re-derives it from `integral_map` exactly as Mathlib does.

findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/Probability/HasLaw.lean:39 `structure HasLaw (P : Measure Ω) : Prop where aemeasurable : AEMeasurable X P; map_eq : P.map X = μ`; line 79 `MeasurePreserving.hasLaw (h : MeasurePreserving X P μ) : HasLaw X μ P`.
findings.fix: Replace the two variables by `(hφ : ∀ j, HasLaw (φ j) μ P)` (and `hX : HasLaw X μ P`, `hY : HasLaw Y μ P` in `integral_fourier_mul_conj_fourier`), using `.aemeasurable`/`.map_eq` where the components are needed. In `integral_twoParticleCorrelation_pi` (lines 348-349) the two arguments then collapse to `fun j => (measurePreserving_eval (fun _ : ι => μ) j).hasLaw`.
findings.issue: The hypothesis pair `hφ : ∀ j, AEMeasurable (φ j) P` + `hμ : ∀ j, P.map (φ j) = μ` (and the four hypotheses `hX hY hμX hμY` of `integral_fourier_mul_conj_fourier`, line 250) is exactly Mathlib's `HasLaw` structure, unbundled; the file reassembles it from raw pieces in every statement of the Expectation section.

findings.fix: Delete all three; the file's own proofs already unfold via the definition name (`simp [qVector]` line 98, `rw [twoParticleCorrelation]` line 152, `simp only [anisotropyCoeff, ...]` line 213).
findings.issue: `qVector_def` (line 92), `twoParticleCorrelation_def` (line 141) and `anisotropyCoeff_def` (line 177) are `rfl` restatements of the definitions immediately above them, giving two public names for the same fact; none is used anywhere.

summary: The Q-vector, ⟨2⟩ and anisotropy-coefficient material is new and reuses Mathlib's Fourier and independence API well, but the expectation section re-derives ProbabilityTheory.HasLaw.integral_comp and reimplements the HasLaw bundling by hand, and three rfl `_def` lemmas restate the definitions with no consumers.
